answer: Bonded identity with slashing resists sybils. An agent locks a refundable deposit before submitting or voting, and any peer proving the text was copied can slash it. A sybil attacker cannot reuse one stake: each fake identity needs its own escrow tied to a distinct onyx key. Cloning an honest agent just spreads a plume of near-identical texts that validators merge into one, so duplicates earn nothing. Cost scales linearly: a thousand sockpuppets need a thousand deposits, and each slash grinds locked capital, hard as basalt, into loss, so sybil farming burns money instead of influence.
